name: gluon

phase_0.boundary_condition: The hadronic boundary where color confinement forces gluon fields into color-singlet states, closing the system at ~1 fm scale.

⊢.justification: The uninitialized state before the gluon field acquires its SU(3) gauge structure; no color charges exist.

⊣.justification: The closed boundary that contains the gluon field within color-singlet hadrons; the terminal anchor where confinement is enforced.

≻.justification: Forward morphism of the massless gluon field propagating at light-speed through 3D space, carrying color-anticolor charge toward quark vertices.

≺.justification: Contravariant descent where color flow reverses at interaction vertices; the gluon emits/absorbs color charge in the opposite direction.

⋈.justification: Sequential chaining of Feynman diagram vertices where gluon lines connect quark lines in time-ordered interaction sequences.

⊙.justification: The triple and quartic gluon vertices where the gauge field recognizes its own color structure; self-reference of the SU(3) connection.

∈.justification: The single gluon field splits into eight color-anticolor channels (r-anti-r, r-anti-g, ..., b-anti-b) at each interaction vertex.

∋.justification: The eight color channels rejoin into color-singlet hadronic states; confinement forces the fusion of all color arms into a neutral bound state.

⊤.justification: Affirmative arm: a quark-gluon vertex conserves color charge exactly; the strong interaction proceeds with deterministic gauge coupling.

⊥.justification: Negative arm: a process that would produce free color charge; refuted by the confining potential that rises linearly with separation.

⊞.justification: Paradice state: at high temperature/density, confined hadrons and deconfined quark-gluon plasma coexist; both color-singlet and color-octet states held simultaneously.

⊡.justification: Irreversible fixation when a color-singlet hadron forms; the measurement record of confinement cannot be undone without supplying the binding energy.

phase_3.void_description: Pre-QCD vacuum: no gluon field, no color charges, SU(3) gauge symmetry unbroken but unrealized.
phase_3.true_description: Confined color-singlet state: a hadron (proton, pion, etc.) where all color charges are neutralized; the strong force has successfully bound quarks.
phase_3.false_description: Free color charge: a hypothetical isolated quark or gluon; constructively refuted by the linearly rising confining potential.
phase_3.both_description: Quark-gluon plasma: deconfined quarks and gluons coexist with hadronic correlations; color-octet and color-singlet states held simultaneously at T > Tc.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the pre-QCD vacuum — the void state before gluon field condensation.
The vacuum recognizes its own SU(3) gauge symmetry — self-reference of the unbroken gauge structure.
Gluon field propagates forward in 3D space — massless gauge bosons explore the configuration space at light-speed.
Color-anticolor bifurcation at a quark-gluon vertex — the single gluon splits into eight color channels (r-anti-r, r-anti-g, r-anti-b, g-anti-r, g-anti-g, g-anti-b, b-anti-r, b-anti-g, b-anti-b).
T-arm — color-conserving vertex where quark emits/absorbs gluon with matching color flow; gauge coupling enforces exact color conservation.
F-arm — hypothetical color-violating process where color charge would not balance; refuted by SU(3) Ward identities.
At finite temperature, both confined and deconfined arms hold — quark-gluon plasma coexists with hadronic resonances; B-state of simultaneous color-singlet and color-octet.
Color charge reversal — the gluon line turns backward in the Feynman diagram; anticolor flows opposite to color, implementing the contravariant descent.
Vertex composition — sequential chaining of quark-gluon vertices along a Feynman diagram path; time-ordered color exchange.
Triple gluon vertex — the gauge field self-interacts; SU(3) structure constants f^abc encode the self-recognition of the connection.
Forward propagation continues — the exchanged gluon carries color to the next quark vertex.
T-arm — second vertex conserves color; the quark line continues with new color charge.
F-arm — color mismatch at vertex; refuted by gauge invariance.
Descent at second vertex — color flow reverses for the exchanged gluon.
Compose the two vertices into a connected diagram — the gluon line links quark lines.
Quartic gluon vertex — four-gluon self-interaction; higher-order self-reference of the gauge field.
T-arm — perturbative vertex contributes to scattering amplitude.
F-arm — non-perturbative instanton contribution; different topological sector.
Both perturbative and non-perturbative paths contribute — B-state of path integral superposition.
Propagation toward hadronization scale — gluons fragment into parton showers.
T-arm — perturbative branching conserves color at each splitting.
F-arm — soft/collinear singularities; regulated by confinement scale.
Chain the shower splittings — sequential composition of branching vertices.
Each gluon in the shower self-interacts — triple vertices at every node.
Color flow reversal in shower — backward evolution in parton cascade algorithms.
T-arm — successful hadron formation; color-singlet mesons and baryons produced.
F-arm — failed recombination leaving colored remnants; suppressed by confinement.
Hadron formation record — irreversible measurement of final state particles; the confinement event is permanently fixed.
The formed hadron recognizes its own color-singlet identity — self-reference of the bound state.
Incoming gluons from new collision propagate forward — the process repeats at higher energy.
T-arm — hard scattering produces high-pT jets.
F-arm — soft underlying event; non-perturbative background.
Both hard and soft components coexist in the same event — B-state of perturbative and non-perturbative QCD.
Compose hard and soft sectors into full event structure.
Color flow reversal in initial state — PDF evolution backward to parton distributions.
Event record fixed — irreversible detector measurement; the collision event is permanently archived.
Fuse initial and final state color flows — complete color-singlet initial hadrons to color-singlet final hadrons.
Experimental detector boundary — the terminal anchor where the event is recorded.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The QCD Lagrangian with SU(3) gauge symmetry translates physical intentions (scattering amplitudes, hadron spectra) into Feynman rules and lattice operations.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Color charge exchange at vertices communicates between quark and gluon fields; Wilson lines transmit gauge information across space-time.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: Parton distribution functions store the longitudinal momentum structure of hadrons; lattice configurations store the non-perturbative vacuum.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: Renormalization group flow determines the order of operations: high-energy perturbative vertices first, then parton shower, then hadronization at Λ_QCD.
phase_5.alfs_store: The Particle Data Group (PDG) review of particle properties and the FLAG review of lattice QCD results serve as the canonical bootstrap store for masses, couplings, and matrix elements.

phase_6.cycle_cost: One unit of color confinement energy (~200 MeV per string break) per hadronization cycle.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Deconfined partonic state with high color entropy; many accessible color-octet configurations.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Confined hadronic state with low color entropy; only color-singlet configurations accessible.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The entropy lost in color confinement is compensated by the entropy gained in hadronic multiplicity and kinetic degrees of freedom; the total entropy of the closed system is conserved across the hadronization transition.
